(frog-profile)=
# frog-profile

<!-- Generated by generate_readme.py from the CLI definitions in src/frogchem/cli. Do not edit by hand. -->

{bdg-danger}`Thermochemistry` Plot reaction energy profiles from TXT, YAML or JSON input files.

## What it does

Draws a publication-style reaction energy diagram from energies you have already computed:
one or more pathways, branches that leave a common trunk, labelled states, highlighted
transition states and section brackets. Use it when the quick plot of `frog-autoprofile`
is not enough, e.g. to compare two mechanisms on one figure or to prepare a figure for a
paper or a talk.

## How it works

```{include} _parts/frog-profile/how_it_works.md
```

## Input

A small text file with the **relative energies** (usually ΔG in kcal/mol, e.g. from
`frog-rrho` or `frog-autoprofile`) in one of three formats (examples in the Reaction
Profiles user guide):

* **YAML** (`.yaml`, recommended): `steps:` (state names), `pathways:` (each with `name` and
  `energies`, optionally `branch_at`, `color`, `style`), plus options such as `title` and
  `label_points`.
* **TXT**: sections `--# PES` (one line of `;`-separated energies per pathway), `--# LABELS`
  and `--# GRAPHS` (`key : value` options).
* **JSON**: `{"Path A": [0.0, 18.4, -3.2]}` or `{"pathways": {...}}`.

The numbers are plotted as given: no unit conversion is done.

### Arguments

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `file` … |  | Input files (.txt, .yaml or .json) |

**Options**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--style` `{default,presentation,straight}` | `default` | Plot style preset |
| `--point-type` `{hollow,bar,dot,.}` |  | Point marker style |
| `--curviness` `CURVINESS` |  | Curve tension (0 = straight lines; preset value if not given) |
| `--config` `CONFIG` |  | JSON file of style options |
| `--secondary` `SECONDARY` |  | JSON file of series for the right-hand y-axis |
| `--annotations` `ANNOTATIONS` |  | JSON file or JSON string of segment annotations |
| `--point-labels` `POINT_LABELS` |  | JSON file or JSON string of per-point labels |
| `--x` `X` |  | JSON file or JSON string of real x coordinates |
| `--legend-barriers` |  | Append the TS barrier (kcal/mol) to the legend labels |
| `--no-legend-barriers` |  | Do not append TS barriers to the legend labels |
| `--interactive` |  | Launch the terminal wizard to build an input file |
| `--gui` |  | Launch the web GUI (Streamlit) in the browser |

**Plot options**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--fig-format` `{png,svg,pdf,eps}` | `png` | Image format, unless the path already has an extension |
| `--dpi` `DPI` | `300` | Raster resolution of saved plots |
| `--show` |  | Also open the plot in an interactive window |

**Output**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-o`, `--output` `PATH` |  | Plot path, or prefix with several inputs (extension overrides --fig-format) |
| `--out-dir` `DIR` |  | Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input file) |

Shared by every command: `-v/--verbose`, `-q/--quiet` — see [CLI conventions](conventions.md).

## Output

| Kind | Name | When | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plot | `<stem>_profile.png` | always | Reaction profile, next to the input (or --out-dir); -o sets the path (prefix <output>_<stem> with several inputs) |
| Plot | `<directory>/Rxn_profile.png` | `save: true` | Legacy TXT inputs with "save: true" (unless -o is given) |
| File | `<directory>/input.txt` | `save: true` | Copy of the legacy TXT input |

### How to read it

Only a figure (nothing is printed on stdout): the state names along the x axis, each pathway
as a smooth curve through its states (a legend when there are several pathways), and the
energy values written at the points you select with `label_points` (YAML) or `labelpoint`
(TXT), typically the transition states. By default no y-axis frame is drawn (`axes` option).
Example: the model input of the user guide shows 18.4 at TS1 and 12.1/15.8 at TS2 for the two paths.

* Check the printed values against your table: they are the numbers of the input, rounded to
  one decimal.
* Branches (`branch_at: INT` in YAML, `@INT:` in TXT) start at the named state; a branch that
  starts at the first state means the name was not found among the `steps`/labels.
* Several inputs with the same stem (`pes.yaml`, `pes.txt`) write the **same**
  `pes_profile.png`: the last one overwrites the others. Use different names or `-o prefix`.
* Legacy TXT files with `save : true` in `--# GRAPHS` are saved as `<directory>/Rxn_profile.png`
  (directory from the `directory` option, default `reaction`) together with a copy `input.txt`,
  unless `-o` is given.
* `--gui` needs the optional `streamlit` package.

## Step by step

1. Write the input file, e.g. `pes.yaml` with `steps: [R, TS1, INT, TS2, P]` and a pathway `energies: [0.0, 18.4, -3.2, 12.1, -10.5]`.
2. Run `frog-profile pes.yaml`: the figure is saved as `pes_profile.png` next to the input (`--out-dir figs` to put it elsewhere, `-o figure1.svg` to choose the file).
3. Adjust the look: `--style presentation` (bigger fonts) or `--style straight` (straight segments), `--point-type bar` (horizontal bars instead of hollow dots), `--curviness 0` (straight lines).
4. Add the TS barrier to the legend with `--legend-barriers`; extra options can come from JSON files (`--config`, `--annotations`, `--point-labels`, `--secondary`, `--x`).
5. No input yet? `frog-profile --interactive` asks for the data in the terminal and writes the input file for you.

## Full reference

Every option, as printed by `frog-profile --help`:

:::{dropdown} `frog-profile --help`
```text
usage: frog-profile [-h] [-v] [-q] [--style {default,presentation,straight}]
                    [--point-type {hollow,bar,dot,.}] [--curviness CURVINESS] [--config CONFIG]
                    [--secondary SECONDARY] [--annotations ANNOTATIONS]
                    [--point-labels POINT_LABELS] [--x X] [--legend-barriers]
                    [--no-legend-barriers] [--interactive] [--gui] [-o PATH] [--out-dir DIR]
                    [--fig-format {png,svg,pdf,eps}] [--dpi DPI] [--show]
                    [file ...]

Plot reaction energy profiles from TXT, YAML or JSON input files.

Draws Bezier-curve reaction coordinate diagrams with point markers, energy labels, segment
annotations, an optional secondary y-axis and section brackets. One figure is saved per input
file; the look is set by --style and the input's own options.

positional arguments:
  file                          Input files (.txt, .yaml or .json)

options:
  -h, --help                    show this help message and exit
  --style {default,presentation,straight}
                                Plot style preset (default: default)
  --point-type {hollow,bar,dot,.}
                                Point marker style
  --curviness CURVINESS         Curve tension (0 = straight lines; preset value if not given)
  --config CONFIG               JSON file of style options
  --secondary SECONDARY         JSON file of series for the right-hand y-axis
  --annotations ANNOTATIONS     JSON file or JSON string of segment annotations
  --point-labels POINT_LABELS   JSON file or JSON string of per-point labels
  --x X                         JSON file or JSON string of real x coordinates
  --legend-barriers             Append the TS barrier (kcal/mol) to the legend labels
  --no-legend-barriers          Do not append TS barriers to the legend labels
  --interactive                 Launch the terminal wizard to build an input file
  --gui                         Launch the web GUI (Streamlit) in the browser

plot options:
  --fig-format {png,svg,pdf,eps}
                                Image format, unless the path already has an extension (default:
                                png)
  --dpi DPI                     Raster resolution of saved plots (default: 300)
  --show                        Also open the plot in an interactive window

output:
  -v, --verbose                 Enable debug output
  -q, --quiet                   Suppress banner, info and saved-file messages
  -o PATH, --output PATH        Plot path, or prefix with several inputs (extension overrides
                                --fig-format)
  --out-dir DIR                 Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input
                                file)

outputs:
  files (next to each input, or --out-dir):
    <directory>/input.txt       [save: true] Copy of the legacy TXT input
  plots (saved, not shown; --fig-format, --dpi, --show):
    <stem>_profile.png          Reaction profile, next to the input (or --out-dir); -o sets the
                                path (prefix <output>_<stem> with several inputs)
    <directory>/Rxn_profile.png
                                [save: true] Legacy TXT inputs with "save: true" (unless -o is
                                given)

examples:
  frog-profile pes.yaml
      Save pes_profile.png next to pes.yaml
  frog-profile pes.txt -o figure1.svg --style presentation
      SVG with the presentation preset
  frog-profile path_a.json path_b.json -o profiles --fig-format pdf --show
      profiles_path_a.pdf and profiles_path_b.pdf, then open the plot windows

Data go to stdout, messages to stderr. Atom indices are 0-based unless stated otherwise.
Step-by-step guide (what it is for, what you need, what to expect): docs/cli/frog-profile.md.
```
:::
